scope: Obstfeld and Rogoff (1996), Chapter 1: intertemporal trade and the current account balance. Two-period consumer (existence, uniqueness, Euler necessity and sufficiency, flat and tilted consumption), autarky rates, gains from trade and the saving-sign lemma by revealed preference, current-account dynamics with government spending, investment and Fisher separation with a strictly concave PPF, isoelastic and CARA closed forms and limits, two-country world equilibrium (existence, rate between autarky rates, first welfare theorem, log closed forms), duality (Shephard, Slutsky), the optimal tax on foreign borrowing, international labour mobility and the factor-price frontier, Walrasian stability and Marshall-Lerner, and the provable end-of-chapter exercises (1-5, 7, 8).
source: Maurice Obstfeld and Kenneth Rogoff (1996), Foundations of International Macroeconomics, MIT Press, Chapter 1, pp. 1-58.
